name: Balancer v2 Composable Stable Pool rounding exploit (mainnet leg)
race_type_reason: The attacker's creation tx (block 23717397, idx 1) had already landed and drained the pools; Bitfinding replayed the same creation input one block later (23717398, idx 2) to rescue residual balances, so it did not pre-empt anything. Replay confirmed on-chain (3 of 983 words differ).
one_liner: Balancer v2 mainnet: whitehat Bitfinding replayed the attacker's exploit input one block after it landed, rescued about 260 ETH-equivalent in this tx, and returned it to the DAO; a 10% bounty was paid on 2026-01-15.

attack_txs.role: A1: contract creation, exploit in constructor (osETH/WETH and wstETH/WETH pools drained into Vault internal balance); the racing attacker tx
A2: stage-1 withdrawal of 6,587 WETH / 6,851 osETH / 4,260 wstETH from the Vault to the beneficiary

mempool_note: mempool-dumpster covers 2025-11-03 (csv only; no sourcelog published for the month) but neither the attacker's A1 nor any Bitfinding tx is in it (private flow or missed). First-seen of A1 and of the replay is unknown. Only four later attacker txs (A8-A9b) were seen publicly, and they were not pre-empted.

trigger.note: A1 was never seen in the public mempool; Bitfinding reacted to the landed A1 (or a private view of it) one block later. No pre-inclusion first-seen exists.

attacker_block_note: Attacker A1 0x6ed07db1a9fe5c0794d44cd36081d6a6df103fab868cdd75d581e3bd23bc9742 landed at idx 1 of block 23717397 (07:46:47Z, built by Titan); the Bitfinding replay is in the next block, 12 s later.

auction.auction_note: Block 23717398 was delivered by bloxroute-regulated from an unlabelled builder pubkey (bid 18.169 ETH, mostly the 17.602 ETH coinbase payment of the 0x240926d7 backrun at idx 1); the Bitfinding bundle (idx 2-4) paid 2 gwei priority (0.0584 ETH) and no coinbase transfer. For the attacker's own block 23717397 (race_23717397.json): Titan-built, delivered via ultrasound, bid 0.0502 ETH, with the 0xc0ffee445a22 backrun paying 20.596 ETH to the fee recipient at idx 2; the winning block's bids there are not retrievable.

loot.gross_loot_method: Assets taken by the replay contract 0xdb8986fd (created by 0x1dc60f91): 135.856824 WETH and 10.956795 wstETH withdrawn in idx 4 (tx 0x0d6f2d90) plus 105.208208 osETH withdrawn from its Vault internal balance on 2025-11-08 (tx 0xaa52c3a7, a call into the same contract). wstETH valued at stEthPerToken 1.218116 (stETH taken as 1 ETH), osETH at OsTokenVaultController.convertToAssets 1.058132, both eth_call at block 23717398. 45.0152 osETH/wETH-BPT also withdrawn in 0xaa52c3a7 is NOT valued and not in this figure.

captured_native.desc: rescued by the creation-tx replay contract; the weETH, rETH and 0.144 WETH of Bitfinding's ~$964K total came from its later replays at 23717631 and 23717709

loot.aggregate_bitfinding_mainnet_usd_source: BIP-892 'Total Recovered (USD at the time of recovery)', Bitfinding, Ethereum Mainnet: $963,832 (all three replay bundles together, not this tx alone)
loot.loot_note: Scope: the Bitfinding replay of A1 (tx 0x1dc60f91 at idx 2 plus its two follow-up txs at idx 3-4, same EOA and block); coinbase and priority fee are summed over those three txs. Bitfinding paid 2 gwei priority (0.058352 ETH), no coinbase transfer, and received no builder refund (no transfer from the fee recipient to the bot in the block). bot_net is the gross rescued value held before it was returned to the DAO multisig; it is a whitehat rescue, not profit. ETH-equivalents use on-chain exchange rates at block 23717398 (see method) so they are approximate. The attacker's own take (6,587 WETH / 6,851 osETH / 4,260 wstETH in A2) is a different scope.

fate.returned_desc: Bitfinding returned its mainnet recoveries to the DAO multisig: wstETH 10.956795 (block 23722968, 2025-11-04), WETH 136.000912 (block 23722994, 2025-11-04; includes 0.144 WETH from its third replay), osETH 105.208208 (block 23756834, 2025-11-08), plus rETH and weETH from its second replay. Balancer's post-mortem put the total at about $964K ($963,832 in BIP-892). The DAO paid the 10% whitehat bounty to 0xc3C7ccE1962B7a744847933CC3abD50b67ff5402 on 2026-01-15 (tx 0xaa0de3c2, block 24237348). Row-level ETH-equivalents (this tx's three assets only): returned in full = 260.5277; net of the 10% bounty = 234.4749.
fate.bounty_desc: 10% bounty on the whole Bitfinding mainnet return, paid by the DAO 2026-01-15T03:13:23Z (13.6001 WETH, 1.0957 wstETH, 0.6617 weETH, 0.6225 rETH, 10.5208 osETH); the figure here is 10% of this row's 260.5277 ETH-equivalent.

fate.public_statement: Balancer post-mortem (quoted by AMBCrypto): Bitfinding alone front-ran attackers on Ethereum Mainnet for $964,000; BIP-892 lists Bitfinding's mainnet recovery as $963,832 with a 10% bounty.
fate.return_status_rule: returned = everything went back to the victim side except a bounty the victim agreed to or offered; partial = some came back, otherwise; none = known zero within the documented search window; unknown = unresolved

discrepancies: incident.json lists 0x7bb28442 priority_fee_gwei 0.1214/0.1273; the race files show gas price = base fee, i.e. priority fee 0.0 (0.1214 is the base fee of the block).
Bitfinding identity is by exact amount match to BIP-892 (the EOA is not printed there); the whole-incident $963,832 covers three replay bundles, only the first is this row.
Replay diff recomputed from site/raw/rpc-balancer2025 tx inputs: 3 of 983 32-byte words differ (word indexes [1, 895, 896]), matching incident.json.
evidence_notes: Bitfinding creation input vs attacker A1 input: same length (31,427 bytes), 3 of 983 words differ (indexes [1, 895, 896]: beneficiary and owner address constants 0xaa760d53/0x506d1f9e -> 0x5af00b07); recomputed from site/raw/rpc-balancer2025/tx_<hash>.json.

Same call shape on the same pools (0xdacf5fa1 osETH/WETH and 0x93d19926): 12 Vault staticcalls, 2 batchSwap-selector calls, 2 manageUserBalance calls; the idx 4 tx withdraws from the new contract's Vault internal balance (incidents/balancer-2025/race_23717398.json focus txs).

Landing order: A1 at 23717397 idx 1, Bitfinding 23717398 idx 2-4; every replay on the same pool lands in a later block than the attacker, so this is a post-inclusion rescue (post-failure-replay), not pre-emption.

Funds trail: tokentx of 0x5af00b07 shows the Vault paying out to it and the returns to the DAO multisig 0x10a19e7e; the bounty tx 0xaa0de3c2 (2026-01-15) in bal_bitf_bounty_tokentx.json matches BIP-892.
0xc0ffee445a22 backrun at 23717397 idx 2 is an arbitrage next to A1 (tx-level facts only; not c0ffeebabe.eth).
